_note: The three states of the live Codex login (#68, #35) and what the board's free signals say about each. Every record says `observed` (true: seen on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09) or false (ASSUMED: written from the adapter's verdict rules and from Codex's source and docs, never captured). Nothing here comes from an auth.json: the board treats that file as opaque bytes. Logged in, logged out (no auth.json) and unreadable (empty or garbage auth.json) are observed; only the expired/revoked state is assumed, because producing it needs a real login that the server has revoked.

login_status.basis: Observed on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09: `codex login status` printed this line on stderr (not stdout) and exited 0. `login status` has no --json option (its --help lists only -c, --enable, --disable).

rollout.basis: A real token_count event of a working turn on 0.161.0 (box check 86). Only the outer timestamp is added here; the capture was the payload alone.

login_status.basis: Observed on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09, with a scratch CODEX_HOME holding no auth.json (no real account was logged out).
Assumed: login status reports that a login file exists, not that it works, so a dead login is believed to read exactly like a live one.

rollout.basis: ASSUMED error item (event_msg of type error: 401 Unauthorized, refresh token revoked, log out and sign in again), built from Codex's source and docs. No real expired or revoked Codex login has been seen yet.

not_an_auth_failure.text: Error: account/read failed during TUI bootstrap: account/read failed: workspace routing discovery timed out (code -32603)
not_an_auth_failure.basis: Printed once by the 0.161.0 TUI on the box (box check 86) while the network answered slowly; Codex exited back to the shell. A real failure that is NOT a dead login.

not_an_auth_failure.text: WARNING: proceeding, even though we could not create PATH aliases: Refusing to create helper binaries under temporary dir "/tmp"
not_an_auth_failure.basis: Printed by `codex login --device-auth` on 0.161.0 with CODEX_HOME under /tmp (box check 87). A scratch-home probe prints it on stderr beside the real answer.

login_status.stderr_empty_file: Error checking login status: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0
login_status.stderr_garbage_file: Error checking login status: stream did not contain valid UTF-8
login_status.basis: Observed on the box, codex-cli 0.161.0, 2026-10-09, with a scratch CODEX_HOME whose auth.json was empty, then 64 random bytes. The verdict reads this as an error (rc 1 without 'not logged in'), never as logged in.
